Implemented on fk-vm-orphan @ commit 4e06b803e89befc1d463f176b1b8ab60364d63b5 (worktree /tmp/fk-1d, reset to origin/main d101757 first). Design + parkWG finding in cc-notes note be8c834e.

Files: new `cmd/vmstress/decoy.go` (+ dispatch/usage in main.go), new `scripts/vm/scenarios/repro-holder-orphan-reap.sh`, `holdbusy`/`releasebusy` added to `scripts/vm/scenarios/workload.sh`. Both arms in one sibling scenario; repro-holder-crash-orphan.sh untouched.

parkWG finding (from source; scenario also settles it empirically): a busy graceful teardown does NOT park. Handle.Unmount runs unmount(dir,0); an NFS busy mount answers EBUSY within unmountGrace=3s → ErrMountBusy+ErrUnmountWedged (mount.go:341), NOT ErrTeardownPending → parkPendingTeardown (server.go:1404) returns false → sweep keeps the busy row, parkWG.Wait() (server.go:287) returns immediately, holder logs "survived the final sweep" (:294) + "mountd stopped" (:299) and EXITS, leaving the busy mount + orphaned real go-nfsv4. Parking is reserved for an unmount(2) that stalls past unmountGrace (server SIGSTOP), which the busy-fd case does not induce. Arm B bounds the exit at 30s and reports PARK if exceeded.

Local gates GREEN: go vet ./... ; go build ./... ; go build -tags fuse ./... ; scripts/test.sh ./... (all ok); shellcheck clean.

PENDING: in-VM validation (not run here — VM code executes only in the tart guest). Run: scripts/vm/vmctl push && VMCTL_RUN_TIMEOUT_MIN=10 scripts/vm/vmctl run repro-holder-orphan-reap (create+provision first if no guest). Leaving task in_progress until the VM run proves clean.
